source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
3. Detail the testing environment including date, time, and location.
4. Name the appliance and its identifying details such as model number, serial number, and manufacturing date.
5. List the specific safety standards and regulations applicable to this appliance (such as NFPA, IEC, and OSHA).
6. Describe the testing procedures performed, referencing the specific steps from the safety check protocols.
7. Document the results of each test precisely, noting any deviations from the standard requirements.
8. Indicate the precise point of failure, including technical details such as electrical readings, physical damage, or mechanical issues.
9. Take photographs of the failed parts or areas to accompany the written report.
10. Record the names and qualifications of the individuals who conducted and supervised the tests.
11. Provide an analysis of why the appliance failed the safety check, incorporating technical interpretations and any contributing factors.
12. Suggest remedial actions or repairs necessary for the appliance to pass
